ON THE GOSPEL OF SAINT JOHN
FROM THE WORDS: "YOU JUDGE ACCORDING TO THE FLESH. I DO NOT JUDGE ANYONE", UNTIL THESE: "I AM THE ONE WHO WITNESS ABOUT ME, AND THE FATHER ALSO WITNESS ABOUT ME, WHO SENT ME"

1. Of the four Gospels, or better, of the four books of the same Gospel, the apostle Saint John, deservedly compared to the eagle in a spiritual sense, is the one who has raised his exposition to a higher and more sublime degree, which, laughingly, also elevates our hearts. The other three evangelists spoke of the Lord as a man passing through the earth, and said little about his divinity. But this one, as if feeling disgusted with crawling on the earth, as he expressed in the beginning of his Gospel, rose not only above the earth and above the air and celestial spaces, but above the angelic squadrons and invisible powers themselves, reaching Him by whom all things were made, saying: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning in God. Through Him all things were made, and nothing was made without Him. He said things in keeping with this beginning, speaking of the divinity of the Lord as no one else has spoken. He returned the water, which he had drunk, since it is not in vain that it is said of him in this same Gospel that at the Supper he

He secretly drank from that breast, and what he secretly drank, he publicly returned with the purpose that all people would not only know the incarnation, passion and resurrection of the Son of God, but also know that before the incarnation there existed the Only Begotten of the Father, the Word of the Father, coeternal with Him who begot him and equal to Him who sent him, made lesser in the very mission so that the Father would be greater. 2. Concerning what you have heard written about the humiliation of Our Lord Jesus Christ, you must consider the mercy in taking our flesh; what came to be done for us, not what was, when he created us. But keep in mind that whatever in the Gospel you read or hear about sublime, divine, elevated above all creatures, about his equality and coeternity with the Father, applied to Him, you hear or read what belongs to the form of God and not what belongs to the form of a servant. And if you follow this rule, as many as you can understand it, since not all of you can understand it, but you must all believe it, if you follow this rule, you will fight safely, like someone who walks in the light, against the slanders of dark heresies. There was no shortage of those who, reading only the evangelical testimonies, admitted those concerning the humiliation of Christ, turning deaf to those referring to his divinity. As deaf as bad readers. Others, focusing only on what is said about the excellence of Christ, although they read that his mercy led him to become man for us, did not believe it, and took these testimonies as false and interspersed by men, sine causa de illo in isto ipso Gospel narratur, quia et in convivio super pectus Domini discumbebat (lo 13,23). De illo ergo pectore in secreto bibebat: sed quod in secreto bibit, in manifesto eructavit, ut perveniat ad omnes gentes non solum incarnatio Filii Dei, et passio, et resurrectio; sed etiam quid etat ante incarnationem Unicus Patri, Verbum Patris, coaetemus generati, aequalis ei a quo missus est; sed in ipsa missione minor factus, quo maior esset Pater. 2.

Quidquid ergo humiliter positum audistis of Domino Iesu Christo, susceptae camis dispensationem cogitate; qualis factus est propter nos, non qualis erat ut faceret nos: quidquid autem sublime et supra omnes creatuias excelsum atque divinum, et Patri aequale atque coaeternum de ¡lio audietitis in Evangelio poní, vel legeritis, scitote vos hoc legere quod ad formara Dei pertinet, non quod ad formam servi. Quia si istam legulam tenueritis qui cápete potestis; non autem omnes cápete potestis, sed omnes ciedeie debentis: si ergo hanc regulam tenueritis, adversus calumnias tenebrarum haereticarum, tanquam in lumine ambulantes, secuii pugnabitis. Non enim defuerunt qui sola evangélica testimonia legendo sectarentur, quae de humilitate Chtisti posita sunt, qui adversus ea testimonia quae divinitatem eius locuta sunt, surdi fuerunt: ideo sutdi, ut male verbosi. item quídam illa sola attendentes quae de Domini sublimitate dicta sunt, etiam ipsi misericotdiam eius, qua homo factus est propter nos, et si legerunt, non ctediderunt, et ab hominibus inducta,

affirming that Our Lord Jesus Christ was only God and not man. Both one and the other all fell into the heresy. But the Catholic Church, holding the doctrine it possesses to be true in every sense and another point and preaching what it believes, saw God and man in Christ. Both things were written and both are true. If you say that Christ is only God, you deny the medicine that has saved you; If you say that he is only a man, you deny the power that has created you. Therefore, hold both things true, a faithful soul and a Catholic heart; Believe them both and confess them faithfully. Christ is God, and Christ is also man. What God is Christ? Equal to the Father, one and the same with the Father. What man is Christ? He was born of a virgin, taking mortality from man without contracting sin. 3. Therefore, these Jews saw man without understanding or believing that he was God. You have already heard how, among other things, they told him: You testify about yourself, your testimony is not true. And in yesterday's reading, which I explained to you according to my ability, you heard the Lord's response. Today these words of his have been read: You judge according to the flesh; That is why you tell me: You testify about yourself, your testimony is not true; because you judge according to the flesh. You do not see God in me, but only man; and by persecuting man, you offend God, hidden in this man. You judge, then, according to the flesh. You will call me bold, because I testify about myself, since the man who gives laudable testimony about himself is described as haughty and arrogant. It is written: Let not your tongue praise you, but that of your neighbor. But this was said of men, that we are weak and speak with weak people. We can tell the truth or lie, and although we must tell the truth, we can nevertheless lie when we want. The Light cannot lie; It is not possible to think that in the brilliance of divine light the darkness of lies can take place. He spoke as Light, he spoke as Truth, and the light shone in the darkness, but they did not understand it. That is why they judged according to the flesh. You, he says, judge according to the flesh. 4. I don't judge anyone. But is it that Christ, our Lord, should not judge anyone? Is it not He whom we confess that he rose again on the third day, that he ascended into heaven, that from there he will come to judge the living and the dead? Is not this our belief of which the Apostle says: It is necessary to have faith in the heart to be justified, and it is necessary to confess it with the word to be saved? Do we contradict the Lord with our confession? We say that He will come as judge of the living and the dead, and He says: I judge no one. This question has two solutions. One: I do not judge anyone now, as it says elsewhere: I have not come to judge the world, but to save it. He does not deny the trial, he postpones it. Another: As he had said: You judge according to the flesh, adding: I do not judge anyone, you can understand, according to the flesh. There should not be any doubt in our hearts contrary to the faith that we have and profess in Christ et superbus videtur. Ideo scriptum est, Non te laudet os tuum, sed laudet te os proximi tui (Prov 27,2). Sed hoc homini dictum est. Infirmi enim sumus, et apud infirmos loquimur. Verum dicere et lieri possumus: etsi verum dicere debenmus, et lieri tamen possumus cum volumus. Lux lieri non potest: absit ut in lucis divinae splendore tenebrae mendacii reperiantur. Loquebatur ille tanquam lux, loquebatur tanquam veritas; sed iux in tenebris luzbat, et tenebrae eam non comprehenderunt: ideo secundum carnem iudicabant. Vos, inquit, secimdum carnem iudicatis. 4. Ego does not indicate quemquam. Non ergo iudicat quemquam Dominus Iesus Christus? Nonne ipse est quem confitemur resurrexisse tertia die, ascendisse in caelum, ibi sedere ad dexteram Patris, inde esse venturum ad iudicandos vivos et mortuos? Nonne ipsa est fides nostra, de qua dicit Apostolus, Corde creditur ad iustitiam, ore autem confessio jit ad salutem? (Rom 10,10). Ergo quando ista confitemur, contra Dominum loquimur?

Nos dicimus venturum iudicem vivorum et mortuorum; ipse autem dicit, Ego non indico quemquam. Quaestio ista duobus modis solvi potest; ut aut hoc imelligamus, non indico quemquam, id est, moda: sicut dicit alio loco, Ego non veni ut iudicem mundum, sed ut salvum jaciam mundum (lo 12,47); non iudicium suum denying, sed differendo. Aut certe quia dixerat, Vos secundum carnem iudicatis; ita subiunxit, Ego non indico quemquam, ut subaudias, secundum carnem. Nullus ergo nobis contra fidem quam tenemus et annuntiamus de iudice Christo, scrupulus dubitationis in corde remaneat. Venit Christus, be salutary cousin

as a judge. Christ came first to save and then to judge, condemning in his judgment those who did not want to be saved and leading to life those who did not reject their salvation. The first function of Our Lord Jesus Christ is medicinal, not judicial. Because, if he had come first to judge, he would not have found anyone to reward justly. But, because he saw that all were sinners and that absolutely no one was exempt from the death deserved by sin, he had to first pour out his mercy to later exercise his justice, as it is said of him in the Psalm: I will sing, Lord, your mercy and your justice. It does not say your justice and your mercy; because, if justice preceded, there would be no room for mercy, and thus, mercy comes first and justice follows. What did mercy do first? The Creator of man deigned to become man. What He had made was done, so that what He had made would not perish. What more can be added to this mercy? He, however, added more. It was little to become a man, he wanted to be despised by man; It was not enough to be despised, he wanted to be dishonored; It was still not enough to be disgraced, he wanted to be put to death; and as if this were not enough, die on a cross. The Apostle wanting to praise his obedience until death, was not content with saying: Made obedient until death, not until any death, but added: Until death on a cross. Among all the deaths, none was worse than death on a cross. For this reason, when the pain is very intense, it is called cruciatus, derived from the word cross. Those crucified, hanging from a tree, with their hands and feet pierced with nails, ended with a very slow death, because vare, postea iudicare: eos iudicando in poenam, qui salvari noluerunt; eos perducendo ad vitam, qui credendo salutem non respuerunt. Prima ergo dispensed Domini nostri Iesu Christi medicinalis est, non iudicialis: nam si primo venisset iudicaturus, neminem invenisset cui praemia iustitiae redderet. Quia ergo vidit omnes peccatores, et omnino neminem esse immunem a morte peccati; prius erat eius misericordia praeroganda, et post exserendum iudicium: quia de illo cantaverat Psalmus, Misericordiam et iudicium cantabo tibi, Domine (Ps 100,1). Non enim iudicium ait et misericordiam; nam si primo esset iudicium, mile esset mercy: sed primo mercy, post iudicium. Who is cousin mercy?

Creator hominis, homo esse dignitus est: factus est quod fecerat, ne periret quem fecerat. Quid huic misericordiae addi potest? And also addidit. Patum fuet ei hominem fieri; sed etiam ab hominibus leprobari: parum erat reprobari; et exhonorari: parum erat exhonorari; et occidi: sed et hoc parum est; morte crucis Nam et cum eius obedientiam usque ad mortem factam commendaret Apostolus, parum illi Fuit dicere, Factus obediens usque ad mortem: non enim qualemcumque mortem, sed addidit, mortem, autem crucis (Phil 2,8). Death was not immediate after crucifixion. They were made to live for a long time on the cross, not in order to lengthen their lives, but in order that, by dying slowly, their torment would be longer. It is an understatement to say that he wanted to die for us; He also wanted to be crucified, becoming obedient to the point of death on a cross. He who was to conquer death, chose the worst and most ignominious kind of death, and, suffering the worst of deaths, made death die. She was terrible in the eyes of the Jews, but she had been chosen by Christ. He had to take his same cross as his standard and had to place it on the foreheads of his faithful as a trophy of his victory over the devil. He who knows everything, when he says maybe, does not doubt, but rebukes. You will see how he says the word perhaps in a reprehensible tone, which seems like a word that expresses doubt. This word expresses doubt when it is said by a man who doubts precisely because he does not know. But said by God, who knows everything, that expression of doubt is a reproach for infidelity, it is not an opinion of Divinity. Even men sometimes doubt things that they hold to be true in a disbelieving tone, that is, they say a word that expresses doubt, even when deep down they do not doubt. Thus, indignant against your servant, you say to him: You do not pay attention to me, realize that perhaps I am your master. For this reason the Apostle, addressing some of his detractors, says to them: It seems to me that I have the spirit of God. When he says it seems to me, he seems to doubt. It is evil not to seek the soul of Christ, but in the way that the disciples sought it, and it is also evil to seek the soul of Christ in the way that the Jews sought it; those to have it, these to lose it. These, seeking it in an evil way, with a perverse intention, heard what follows: You will search for me, and, lest you believe that you will search for me with a good intention, you will die in your sin. Verumtamen si per aliquam infirmitatem adhuc te delectat mundus, habitet in te qui mundat, et eris mundus. Omnes enim cum peccato nati sumus; omnes vivir ad id quod nati eramus addidimus, magisque de mundo facti sumus, quam tune quando de parentibus nostris nati sumus. Et ubi essemus, si ille non vinoet, qui non habebat omnino peccatum, ut solveret omne peccatum? In quem Iudaei quia non ctedebant, merit audierunt, Moriemini in peccatis vesS.As. 14
About the Gospel of Saint John

has not even a shadow of sin, had he not come to destroy all sin? The Jews, for not believing in EJ, were justly sentenced: You will die in your sins. Since it was not possible for you to be exempt from all sin, having been born with it, however, if you had believed in me, you would certainly have been born in sin, but you would not die in sin. The whole misfortune, then, of the Jews lies not in being born with sin, but in dying with their sins. This is the misfortune that every Christian must avoid, for which baptism is resorted to, and those who, due to their weakness or for other reasons, are in danger, ask to be helped; For this reason, even the nursing child is carried in the pious arms of the mother to the Church, so that it does not leave without baptism nor die with the sin with which it was born. A most unhappy state and miserable fate is that of those who heard from the mouth of the Truth: You will die in your sins. 7. However, he gives them the reason why this happens, saying to them: If you do not believe that I am what I am, you will die in your sins. I believe, brothers, that in that crowd that listened to the Lord there were also those who would believe. And as if that very severe sentence had been issued against everyone: You will die in your sins, and the doors to hope were closed even for those who were to believe, some became enraged, others feared, or better yet, they did not fear, they were already in despair. The Lord restored hope to them, adding: If you do not believe that I am he, you will die in your sins. Therefore, if you believe that I am he, you will not die in your sins. Hope returned to the desperate, activity to the sleeping: the cotris: quia non habere peccatum nullo moda potuistis, qui cum peccato nati estis, sed tamen si in me, inquit, credideritis, cum peccato quidem nati estis, sed in peccato vestro morituri non estis. Tota ergo infelicitas Iudaeorum ipsa erat, non, peccatum habere, sed in peccatis mori. Hoc est quod deben fugere omnis christianus: propter hoc ad Baptismum curritur; propter hoc qui aegritudine vel aliunde periclitantur, sibi desiderant subveniri; propter hoc etiam sugens parvulus a matre piis manibus ad Ecclesiam fertur, ne sine Baptismo exeat, et in peccato quo natus est moriatur. Infelicissima conditio, misera sors istorum, qui de ore verídico audierunt, In peccatis vestris moriemini. 7.

Unde tamen hoc eis contingat, exonit: Si enim non credideritis quia ego sum, moriemini in peccatis vestris. Credo, fratres, in illa multitudine quae Dominum audiebat, et eos fuesse qui credituri weret. Quasi autem in omnes processerat severissima illa sententia, ln peccato vestro -moriemini; ac per hoc et illis qui credituri erat, spes erat ablata: illi saeviebam, illi timebant; imo non timebant, sed iam desperate. Revoke eos in spem; adiunxit enim, Si non credideritis quia ego sum, moriemini in peccatis vestris. Ergo si credideritis quia ego sum, non moriemini in peccatis vestris. Reddita est spes desperantibus, excitatio facta est dormientibus, cordibus evigilaverunt: inde plurimi ctediderunt, sicut Evangelii ipsius consequentia testantur. Erant enim illic membra Christi,
About the Gospel of Saint }uart

Reason was put on guard, and many believed, as can be deduced from the following words of the same Gospel. There were members of Christ who had not yet joined the body of Christ; And among the people who crucified him, who hung him on the cross, who mocked him by hanging on it, who wounded him with the spear, who gave him gall and vinegar to drink, there were members of Christ, for whom he said: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do. And what will a convert fail to forgive himself if it is the shed blood of Christ that asks for forgiveness? What murderer can despair if Christ gave hope to the same person who gave him death? For this reason many believed. The blood of Christ was shed so that, by drinking it, they would have something to rescue themselves, rather than fear becoming guilty of having shed it. Who can despair? Do not be surprised that on the cross a thief, shortly before a murderer, shortly after accused, convicted, condemned, suspended, released, is saved. Where he was convicted, there he was condemned; but there he was changed, there he was set free. Thus, among the crowd to whom the Lord spoke were those who were to die in their sin and those who, believing in the same one who spoke to them, were to be freed from all sin. 8. However, pay attention to what Christ our Lord says: If you do not believe that I am He, you will die in your sins. What does it mean: If you do not believe that I am he, you will die in your sins? I am, what? He added nothing; And because he added nothing, he hinted a lot. What was he expected to say? Perhaps: if you do not believe that I am Christ; if you do not believe that I am quae nondum adhaeserant corpori Christi: et in illo populo a quo crucifixus est, a quo in ligno suspensus est, a quo pendens inisus est, a quo lancea vulneratus est, a quo felle et aceto potatus est, werent membra Christi, pro quibus dixit, Pater, ignosce illis, quia nesciunt quid faciunt. Quid autem converso non ignoscitur, si iusus Christi sanguis ignoscitur? Quis homicidal desperet, si in spem redditus est a quo etiam Christus occisus est? Crediderunt inde multi; donatus est eis sanguis Christi, m magis eum biberent quo liberaentur, quam rei de illo effuso tenerentur: quis desperet?

Et si in cruz latro salvatus est, ante paululum homicida, post paululum accusatus, convictus, damnatus, suspensus, liberatus; noli mirari. Ubi convictus, ibi damnatus: sed ibi liberatus, ubi mutatus (Luke 23:34-43). In hoc ergo populo cui Dominus loquebatur, weret who in sin suo fuent morituri: weret etiam who in ipsum qui loquebatur, werent credituri, et ab omni peccato libeiandi. 8. Tamen hoc attende quod ait Dominus Christus: Si non credideritis quia ego sum, moriemini in peccatis vestris. Quid est, Si non credideritis quia ego sum? Ego sum, what? Nihil addidit; et quia nihil addidit, multum est quod commendavit. Exspectabatuí enim ut diceret quid esset, nec tamen dixit. Quid expectabatuí ut dieexet? Forte, Nisi credideritis quia ego sum Christus; nisi credideritis quia ego sum Dei
About the Gospel of Saint John

the Son of God; if you do not believe that I am the Word of the Father: if you do not believe that I am the Creator of the world; or if you do not believe that I am the Former and Reformer of man, the Builder and repairer, the Maker and Sustainer; If you do not believe that I am all this, you will die in your sins. This word contains many things: I am, as he had said to Moses: I am who I am. Who can conveniently explain the meaning of the word am? Through his angel God sent Moses to free his people from Egypt (you already know this from having read and heard it; but I remind you). Moses trembled, excused himself and obeyed. Excusing himself, he said to God, who was speaking through his angel: If the people ask me who is the God who sent you, what will I answer? And the Lord says to him: I am who I am; and he repeated it to them: You will say to the children of Israel: He who is has sent me to you. It does not say: I am God, or I am the maker of the world; o I am the creator of all things; o I am the one who multiplies the people that you are going to liberate, but simply: I am who I am; and you will say to the children of Israel: He who is. He did not add: He who is your God, he who is the God of your fathers, but only said: He who is sent me to you. Perhaps it was a lot for Moses himself, as it is also a lot for us, and especially for us to understand the meaning of I am who I am, and of He who is sent me to you. And if Moses understood it, when would those to whom he was sent understand it? So the Lord differed what man could not understand, and added what he could understand: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God Philius; nisi credideritis quia ego sum Verbum Patris; nisi credideriiis quia ego sum conditor mundi; nisi credideritis quia ego sum hominis formator et reformator, creator et recreator, factor et refactor: nisi hoc credideritis quia ego sum, moriemini in peccatis vestris. Multum est quod ait ipsum, Ego sum: quia sic dixerat et Deus Moysi, Ego sum qui sum. Quis digne eloquatur quid sit, sum? Mittebat Deus per angelum suum, servum suum Moysen ad liberandum ex Aegypto populum suum (legistis quod audistis, et nostis; commemoro tamen); mittebat trementem; excusentem, be obedientem. Cum ergo excusaret, ait Deo, quem loqui in angelo intelligebat: Si dixerit mihi populus, Et quis est Deus qui misit te, quid eis dicam? Et Dominus ad eum, Ego sum qui sum: et repetivit, You say jiliis Israel, Qui est, misit me ad vos.

Non ait et ibi, Ego sum Deus; aut, Ego sum mundi fabricator; aut, Ego sum omnium rerum creator; aut, Ego sum ipsius populi liberandi propagator: sed hoc tantum, Ego sum qui sum; et, You say jiliis Israel, Who is; non addidit, Qui est Deus vester, qui est Deus patrum vestrorum, sed tantum hoc dixit, Qui est, misit me ad vos. Forte multum erat et ad ipsum Moysen, sicut multum est et ad nos, et multo magis ad nos, intelligere quid dictum sit, Ego sum qui sum; et, Qui est, misit me ad vos. Et si forte caperet Moyses, illi ad quos mittebatur when caperent? Distulit ergo Dominus quod capere homo non posset. et addidit quod capere posset: adiunxit enim
About the Gospel of Saint John

of Jacob. You can understand this, because what intelligence can understand I am who I am? 9. What will we do? Will we dare to say anything about what the Lord said: I am who I am; or rather about what you heard him say: If you do not believe that I am He, you will die in your sins? And I, with my strength so scarce and almost null, will I dare to reason what is said by Our Lord Jesus Christ: If you do not believe that I am? Will I dare to ask the Lord himself? Listen to me asking, rather than reasoning, seeking rather than presuming, learning rather than teaching, and with me and through me you also ask. Soon the Lord is also there, who is everywhere. Listen to the affection of the questioner, and grant the power to understand. Well, with what words can I bring to your hearts what I understand, if I can understand anything? What voices will be enough? What eloquence will be enough? What forces to understand it? What power to declare it? 10. I will speak to Our Lord Jesus Christ, I will speak, and He will hear me. I believe He is present, I have not the slightest doubt, for He said: Behold, I am with you until the end of the ages. O Lord our God, what do you say: If you do not believe that I am He? What is there that is not from what you did? Isn't it heaven? Isn't it the earth? Are they not the things that are in heaven and on earth? Isn't that the man you're talking to? Is it not the angel you send? If all these are coet ait, Ego sum Deus Abraham, the Deus Isaac, et Deus lacob (Ex 3,13-15). Hoc potes capere: Nam Ego sum qui sum, quae mens potest capere? 9. Quid ergo us? audebimusne aliquid dicere ex hoc quod dictum est, Ego sum qui sum: vel potius ex hoc quod Dominum dicere audistis, Nisi credideritis quia ego sum, moriemini in peccatis vestris? Itane his viribus meis tantillis et penis nullis, audebo disputare quid sit quod ait Dominus Christus, Nisi credideritis quia ego sum? Audebo ipsum Dominum intertogare: audite me interrogantem potius quam disputantem, magis quaerentem quam praesumentem, potius discentem quam docent, et certe in me vel per me etiam vos interrógate. Praesto est etiam ipse Dominus qui ubique est, audit interrogandi affectum, et intelligendi praestet effectum. Nam ego quibus verbis, et si forte aliquid cajjio, perducere possum quod capio ad corda vestra? Quisnam sufficit sonus? What suppetit eloquentia? quae vires intelligendi? What faculties did you utter? 10.

Dicam ergo Domino nostro Iesu Christo, dicam, et audit me. Credo ptaesentem, omnino non dubito; ipse enim dixit, Ecce ego vobiseum sum usque in consummationem saecwli (Mt 28:20). O Domine Deus noster, quid est quod aisti, Nisi credideritis quia ego sum? Quid enim non est eorum quae fecisti? Numquid caelum non est? numquid terra non est? numquid non sunt ea quae in terra et in cáelo sunt? numquid homo ipse cui loqueris non est? numquid angelus quem mittis non est? Si omnia sunt haec quae per te facta sunt, quid est quod cibi pro-
About the Gospel of Saint John

sas, that you did, why did you reserve for yourself the Being itself, as something of your own, which you did not give to anyone in order to be yourself alone? How do I hear: I am what I am, as if other things were not; and how do I hear: If you do not believe that I am? Weren't those who were listening to you? Although sinners, they were men. Well what am I doing? Let it be the Being itself, say it to the heart, say it inside, speak it there, let the inner man hear, and the mind perceives what it truly is; Well, it is always being the same way. A thing, whatever it may be (as I begin to reason and stop questioning; perhaps I want to say what I heard; May He grant exultation to my ears and to yours as I speak), whatever it is, however excellent it may be, if it is mutable, it truly is not, because true being is not there where non-being is. What changes, after the change, is not what it was; If it is not what it was, there has been a death there; something that was and is no longer perished there. The blackness disappeared from the head of an old man, who begins to whiten; beauty died in the body of a worn and bent old man; The strength is dead in a languid body; dead stillness in a walking body; dead the movement in a still body; dead movement and erection in a recumbent body; locution dead in a silent language; In what is changed and is what was not, I see a certain life in what is and a death in what was. Finally, of the man who has died, when the question is asked, Where is that man?, the answer is: He was. Oh truth that you truly are! In all our actions and movements and in all prium quiddam tenuisti ipsum esse, quod alus non dedisti, ut tu solus esses? Nam quomodo audio, Ego sum qui sum; quasi alia non sint? et quomodo audio, Nisi credideritis quia ego sum? lili enim noneront qui audiebant? And if peccatores were, nomines were. Quid etgo fació?

Quid sit ipsum esse, dicat cordi, intus dicat, intus loquatur; homo interior audit, mens capiat veré esse: est enim semper eodem moda esse. (Res enim aliqua, quaelibet omnino: quasi coepi disputare, et destiti quaerere; forte quod audivi voló loqui, auditui meo det exsultationem et vestro cum loquor): res enim quaelibet, prorsus qualicumque excellentia, si mutabilis est, non veré est; non enim est ibi verum esse, ubi est et non esse. Quidquid enim mutari potest, mutatum non est quod erat: si non est quod erat, mors quaedam ibi facta est; peremptum est aliquid ibi quod erat, et non est. Nigredo mortua est in capite albescentis senis, pulchritudo mortua est in corpore fessi et incurvi senis, mortuae sunt vires in corpore languentis, mortua est statio in corpore ambulantis, mortua est ambulatio in corpore statis, mortua est ambulatio et statio in corpore iacentis, mortua est locutio in lingua tacentis: quidquid mutatur et est quod non erat, video ibi quamdam vitam in eo quod est, et mortem in eo quod Fuit: Denique de mortuo cum dicitur, Ubi est homo ille? respondtur, Fuit. O veritas quae veré es! Nam in omnibus actionibus et motibus nostris, et in omni prorsus agitatione creaturae duo tempora in-
About the Gospel of Saint John

The changes of creatures found two times: the past and the future. I look for the present; nothing remains. What I said is no longer; What I am going to say is not yet; what I did is no longer; what I am going to do is not yet; what I have lived is no longer; What I am going to live is not yet. I find the past and the future in every movement of things. In the truth, which remains, I find neither past nor future, but a present, and this incorruptible, which is not found in the creature. Go through the vicissitudes of things, you will find the was and the will be. For so that you too may be, rise higher than time. But who will ascend by his own strength? Take you there He who said to his Father: I want them to be with me where I am. By making this promise to us, so that we may die in our sins, it seems to me that Our Lord Jesus Christ in these words: If you do not believe that I am God, he meant nothing but this: If you do not believe that I am God, you will die in your sins. Let us thank God, because he said: If you do not believe; and he did not say: If you do not understand. Because who can be able to understand it? Or is it that because I have dared to speak to you, and you think I have understood, you will have understood something of such sublime ineffability? If you don't understand it, faith saves you. That is why the Lord did not say: Unless you understand that I am; but he said what men can do: If you do not believe that I am he, you will die in your sins. 11. But they, always fond of earthly things, and always hearing and responding according to the flesh, said to him: Who are you?, because when you said: If you do not believe that I am, I do not agrevenio, praeteritum et futurum. Praesens quaero, nihil stat: quod dixi, iam non est; quod dicturus sum, nondum est: quod feci, iam non est; quod facturus sum, nondum est: quod vixi, iam non est; quod victurus sum, nondum est. Praeteritum et futurum invenio in omni motu terum: in veritate quae manet, praeteritum et futurum non invenio, sed solum praesens, et hoc incorruptibiliter, quod in creatura non est. Discute rerum mutationes, invenies Fuit et Erit: cogita Deum, invenies Est, ubi Fuit et Erit esse non possit. Ut etgo et tu sis, transcende tempus. Sed quis transcendet viribus suis? Levet illuc ille qui Patri dixit, Voló ut ubi ego sum, et ipsi sint mecum.

Hoc itaque promittens ne moriamur in peccatis nostris, nihil aliud Dominus Iesus Christus mihi videtur his verbis dixisse, Nisi credideritis quia ego sum: prorsus nihil aliud mihi videtur his verbis dixisse quam hoc, Nisi credideritis quia ego Deus sum, moriemini in peccatis vestris. Bene, Deo gratias, quia dixit, Nisi credideritis: non dixit, Nisi ceperitis. Quis enim hoc capiat? Aut veré, quia ausus sum dicere, et visi estis intelligere, aliquid de tanta ineffabilitate cepistis? Si ergo non capis, fides te liberat. Ideo et Dominus non ait, Nisi ceperitis quia ego sum; sed quod poterant dixit, Nisi credideritis quia ego sum, moriemini in peccatis vestris. 11. Et illi semper terrena sapientes et semper secundum carnem audientes et responders, quid ei dixerunt? Who is it? Non enim cum dixisti, Nisi credideritis quia ego sum. addidisti quid esses. Quis es, ut
About the Gospel of Saint John

spend what you were. Who are you, so that we believe? And He answers: The Principle, That is, what the Being. The principle does not undergo mutation, it remains in itself and renews all things. Truly it is the beginning of whom it is written: You are always the same, and your years will have no end. I am, he says, the Principle, the same one I am speaking to you about. Believe that I am the Beginning, so that your sins may not die. And since in the question they asked Him they only said: Who are you?, without adding more, He answered: The Beginning, that is, believe that I am the Beginning. This is seen more clearly in Greek than in Latin. In the Greek language the word principle is of the feminine gender, as in Latin law it has a feminine gender, and in Greek it is masculine; On the other hand, wisdom, both in Latin and Greek, is of the feminine gender. The way of speaking varies in each language, the gender of the words, because things lack gender. For wisdom is not really a female, and since Christ is the Wisdom of God, Christ is named in the masculine gender, and wisdom is named in the feminine gender. When the Jews therefore said: Who are you?, He, who knew that among them there were some who had to believe, and who for the same reason had said: Who are you?, so that they would know what they should believe, answered: The Beginning; not as affirming that He was the Beginning, but as saying: Believe Me the Beginning. This, as I said, appears clear in the Greek language, in which principle is of the feminine gender. As if He wanted to say that He was the Truth, and to those who asked, Who are you?, He answered: The Truth. Well, it seems that to the question, Who are you?, should credamus? Et ille, Principium. Ecce quod est esse. Principium mutari non potest: principium in se manet, et innovat omnia; principium est, cui dictum est, Tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non deficient (Ps 101,28). Principium, ait, quia et loquor vobis. Principium me credite, ne moriamini in peccatis vestris. Tanquam enim in eo quod dixerunt, Tu quis es? nihil aliud dixerint quam, Quid te esse credimus? respondit, Principium; id est, Principium me credite. In graeco namque eloquio discernitur, quod non potest in latino.

Apud graecos enim feminini generis est principium, sicut apud nos lex generis feminini est, quae apud illos est masculini: sicut sapientía et apud nos et apud jilos generis feminini est. Consuetudo locutionis ideo per diverse linguas vatiat genera vocabulorum, quia in ipsis rebus non invenís sexum. Non enim sapientia veré femina est, cum Christus sit Dei Sapientia (1 Cor 1,24), et Christus appelletur genere masculine, sapientia feminino. Cum ergo dicerent Iudaei, Your quis es? ille qui sciebat esse ibi quosdam credituros, et ideo dixisse, Tu quis es? ut scirent quid illum ciedere debenent, responder, Principium: non tanquam diceret, Principium sum; sed tanquam diceret, Principium me credite. Quod in sermone graeco, ut dixi, evidentor apparet, ubi feminini generis est principium. Velut si vellet dicete se esse veritatem, et dicetibus, Tu quis es? I will answer:, Veritatem; curo videoatur ad id quod dictum est, Tu quis est? re-
About the Gospel of Saint John

having answered: The Truth; that is: I am the Truth. But he answered louder, seeing that they asked, Who are you?, as if to say: We have heard you say: If you do not believe that I am, what should we believe that you are? To which he responded: Principle; that is, believe me Principle. And he added that I am speaking to you, that is, humbling myself for you, I descended to speak your language. For if, being as it is Principle, he had remained in the Father in such a way that he did not take the form of a servant, and as a man spoke to men, how would they believe him, if the poor heart cannot hear the intelligible Word except through sensitive voices? Therefore, he says, believe that I am the Beginning, for that you may believe, not only am I, but I also speak to you. But there is already a lot that I have told you about this topic. Your Charity allow me, with the help of God, to reserve what is left for tomorrow.

To God" 1. The words that Our Lord Jesus Christ said to the Jews, tempering his language so that the blind would not see and at the same time open the eyes of the faithful, and which have been read today in the holy gospel, are the following: They said to him, then, spondere debuisse, Veritas; id est, Veritas sum. Sed altius respondit, cum videret eos ita dixisse, Tu quis es? ac si dicerent, Quoniam abs te audivimus, Nisi credideritis quia ego sum, quid te esse credemus? ad hoc respondit, Principium: tanquam diceret, Principium me credite. Et addidit, quia et loquor vobis: id est, quia humilis propter vos factus, ad ista verba descendí. Nam si principium sicuti est, ita maneiet apud Patrem, ut non acciperet formam servi et homo loqueretur hominibus; Qumodo ei crederent, cum infirma corda intelligibile Verbum sine voce sensibili audire non possent? Ergo, inquit, credite me esse principium; quia, ut credatis, non solum sum, sed et loquor vobis. Sed de hac re iam multum est loqui vobis: placeat ¡taque Charitati vestrae ut quod restat, illo adiuvante servemus, crastino reddituri.

1. Verba Domini nostri Iesu Christi quae habuit cum Iudaeis, ita moderans loquelam suam, ut caeci non viderent, et fideles oculos aperirent, quae hodie de sancto Evangelio recitata sijnt, ist sunt: Dicebant ergo Iudaei, Tu quis es? Quia dixerat snpra Dominus, Nisi credideritis
About the Gospel of Saint John

Jews, who are you? As the Lord had previously said: If you do not believe that I am, you will die in your sins, they replied: Who are you?, as if asking who they should believe in so as not to die in their sin. To the question: Who are you?, he responded by saying: The Principle, which I speak to you. If the Lord said that He was the Beginning, it may be asked whether the Father is also the Beginning. If the Son, who has a Father, is a Principle, how much easier is it to understand that God the Father is a Principle, who has a Son from whom he is a Father, but has no one from whom he proceeds? The Son is the Son of the Father and the Father is the Father of the Son; but the Son is God from God, light from light. It is said that the Father is light, but not of light; that the Father is God, but not of God. For if the God of God, the light of light, is Principle, how much better will it be understood that the God from whom God proceeds, the light from which light comes, is Principle? Dearest, it seems absurd to say that the Son is Principle and let's not call the Father Principle. 2. What will we say? Will there be two Principles? Be careful saying this. Well what? If the Father is a Principle and the Son is a Principle, how can they not be two Principles? How do we say that the Father is God, that the Son is God, and not say that they are two gods? It is a crime to say two gods, just as it is a crime to say three gods, and yet he who is Father is not Son; He who is the Son is not the Father, and the Holy Spirit, who is the Spirit of the Father and the Son, is neither the Father nor the Son. Nihil enim aliud videtur dixisse, nisi eos post passionem suam cognituros quis esset. Procul dubio ergo videbat ibi aliquos, quos ipse noverat, quos ipse cum caeteris sanctis suis ante constitutionem mundi praesyendo elegetat, post passionem suam esse credituros. Ipsi sunt illi quos assidue commendamus, et ad imitationem cum magna exhortatione proponimus.

Misso enim desuper Spiritu sancto post Domini passionem et resurrectionem et ascensionem, cum miracuta ieront in eius nomine, quem tanquam mortuum petsequentes Iudaei contempserant, compuncti sunt corde; et qui saevientes occiderunt, mutari crediderunt; et quem sanguinem saeviendo fuderunt, credendo biberunt: illa tria millia, et illa quinqué millia Iudaeorum (Act 2,37.41, et 4,4), quos ibi videbat, quando dicebat, Cum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tune cognoscetis quia ego sum. Tanquam dices, Diiferous cognitionem vesttam, ut impleam passionem meam: ordine vestro cognoscetis qui 6Ím. Non quia omnes tune etant credituti ex lis qui audiebant, id est, post passionem Domini: nam paulo post dicit, Haec eo loquenle, vmhi crediderunt in eum, et nondum exaltatus erat Fiiíus hominis. Exaltationem quippe dicit passionis, non glorificationis; crucis, non caeli: quia et ibi exaltatus est, quando pependit in ligno. Sed illa exaltatio humiliatio Fuit. carried out through those who later believed, to whom he says: When you have exalted the Son of man, then you will know that I am he. The Lord knowing these in the midst of that crowd, said: When you have lifted up the Son of man, then you will know that I am he. You already know what I am means, and I am not going to repeat it every step of the way, so that something so lofty does not cause annoyance. Remember: I am that I am, and He that is sent me, and you will know what it means: Then you will know that I am. But the Father is also, and the Holy Spirit is also. The entire Trinity has the same being. But, since the Lord spoke as the Son, to avoid that in these words: Then you will know that I am, the error of the Sabellians or Patripasians could be hidden, which I recommended that you always reject it, that is, the error of those who affirmed that the Father and the Son are the same: they are two names, but one thing. To avoid this error and so that it would not be understood that when He said: Then you will know that I am, He was the Father Himself, then He added: And I do nothing of Myself, but say what the Father has taught me. The Sabellian was already jumping for joy, thinking that he had discovered the key to his error, but as soon as he raised his head in the darkness, he was confused by the light of the following sentence: You imagined that He was the Father, because He said: That I am; hear that He is the Son: And of Myself I make nothing. What does it mean: I do nothing of myself? That of me dituri, quibus dicit, Cum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tune cognoscelis quia ego sum. Quare hoc, nisi ut nemo desperaret in quocumque scelere male sibi conscius, quando videbat eis donari homicidium qui occiderant Christum? 3. Hos ergo in illa turba agnoscens Dominus, dixit, Cum exahaveritis Vilium hominis, tune cognoscetis quia ego sum. Iam nostis quid sit sum; nec assidue repetendum est, ne pariat res tanta fastidium. Recolite illud, Ego sum qui sum, et Qui est, misit me (Ex 3,14); et agnoscetis, quid dictum sit, Tune scietis quia ego sum: sed et, Pater est, et Spiritus sanctus est. Ad ipsum esse pertinet all Trinitas.

Sed quia Dominus sicut Filius loquebatut, ne forte in eo quod dixit, Tuno cognoscetis quia ego sum, subintraret error Sabellianorum, hoc est Patripassianorum, quem vobis errorem commendavi non tenendum, sed cavendum, eorum sálicet qui dixerunt, ípse est Pater, ípse est Filius; duo sunt nomina, sed res una: propter istum ergo cavendum errorem cum díxisset Dominus, Tune cognoscetis quia ego sum; ne ipse intelligeretur Pater, continuous subiunxit, Et a meipso fació nihil, sed sicut ¿oenit me Pater, haec loquor. Iam gaudere coeperat sabellianus, erroris sui eccasione comperta: statim ut se tanquam in obscuro extulit, sequentis sententiae luz confusus est. Putaveras eum esse Patrem, quia dixit, Ego sum: audi quia Filius est, Et a meipso fació nihil. Quid is,

I'm not the same. The Son has to be God from God; but the Father does not have the Son to be God. The Son is God of God; The Father is God, but not of God. None of you, my brothers, let yourself be carried away by carnal thoughts when you hear him say that he speaks what his Father taught him. The shortness of man can only think about things that he is accustomed to do or hear. Never think that they are like two men, one father, the other son, and that the father speaks to the son, as you do when you speak to your son, giving him warnings and instructions about what to say, so that he retains in memory what he has heard from you, and after the memory passes it into his language, and through sounds he makes what he perceived in his own penetrate into the ears of others. Do not have such thoughts, lest your heart become a factory of idols. Do not attribute to the Trinity human form, features of human limbs, figure of human flesh, visible senses, size and bodily movements, use of language, diversity of sounds: all these things belong to the form of a servant that the only begotten Son took when the Word became flesh to live among us. I do not prohibit, but rather I force the weak human being to think about Him what he already knows. If you have true faith, believe that such is Christ; but such from the Virgin Mary, not from God the Father. He was a child, he grew like men, he walked, he had A meipso fació nihil? A meipso non sum. Filius enim de Patre est Deus; Pater autem non est de Filio Deus: Filius est Deus de Deo; Pater autem Deus, sed non de Deo: Filius est lumen de lumine; Pater autem lumen, sed non de lumine: Filius est, sed est de quo est; Pater autem est, sed non est de quo est. 4. Quod ergo addidit, Sicut docuit me Pater, haec loquor; nemini vestrum obrepat cogitatio carnalis, fratres mei. Non enim potest humano infirmitas cogitare, nisi quod consuevit faceré vel audire.

Nolite ergo vobis quasi duos homines ante oculos poneré, ntmm patrem, alterum filium, et loquentem patrem ad filium: sicut facis tu, quando verba aliqua dicis filio tuo, monens eum et instruens eum quomodo loquatur, ut quaecumque audivit a te, comrnendet memoriae; cum commendaverit memoriae, proferat et lingua, distinguat per sonos, inferat auribus alicuius quod percepit in suis. Nolite ita cogitare, ne in corde vestro idola fabricetis. Humanam formam, humanorum lineamenta membrorum, figuram carnis humanoe, sensus istos conspicuos, statuiam motusque corporis, linguae officium, distinctiones sonotum, nolite in illa Trinitate cogitare, nisi quod pertinet ad formam servi, quam accepit unigénitas Filius, cum Verbum caro factum est, ut habitaret in nobis (lo 1,14). Ibi do not prohibit you, humano infirmitas, cogitare quod nosti; imo etiam compello. Si fides in te vera est, talem Christum cogita: sed ex Maria virgine, non de Deo Patre talem cogita, Infans Fuit, ctevit ut homo, ambulavit ut homo, esurivit, sitivit ut homo, dormi-

hunger and thirst, he slept and, finally, he suffered like a man, he was hanged on a tree, died and buried like a man; In the same human form he rose again, ascended to heaven in the sight of his disciples, and in the same form he will come to judgment. It is the voice of the angels, recorded in the Gospel: He will come in the same form that you have seen ascend to heaven. When you look at Christ in the form of a servant, if you have faith, consider the human form But, when you think that In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God, remove from your heart every human figure; remove from your thoughts everything that is enclosed in the limits of matter, everything that occupies a place in space, everything that is subject to measurement; banish such fictions from your heart. Notice, if you can, the beauty of wisdom, consider the beauty of justice. Does it have shape, size, color? It has none of this, and yet it exists, because, if it did not exist, it would not be loved, nor rightly praised, and neither loved nor praised would have a place in the heart and in the customs. Now, there are wise men, and how could they be wise without wisdom? Therefore, O man, if you cannot see your wisdom with the eyes of your body nor imagine it as you imagine corporeal things, will you dare to ascribe the figure of a human body to the Wisdom of God? 5. What shall we say, brothers? How did the Father speak to the Son, for He says: What my Father taught me, that is what I speak? Did he really talk to you? When the Father taught the Son, did he pronounce palavit ut homo, desserto passus ut homo, suspensus in ligno, occisus, sepultus ut homo; in eadem forma resurrexit, in eadem forma ante oculos discipulorum ascendit in caelum, in eadem forma venturus est ad iudicium. Angelorum enim vox est in Gospel expresses: Sic veniet quomodo eum vidistis euntem in caelum (Acts 1,11). Quando ergo de forma servi cogitas in Christo, humanom effigiem cogita, si est in te fides: quando autem cogitas, In principle erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum (lo 1,1), pereat de corde tuo omnis humano figuratio: pellatur de cogitationibus tuis quidquid fine corporeal terminatur, quidquid loci spatio continetut, vel quantalibet mole diffusion; de corde tuo figmentum tale dispereat. Cogita, si potes, pulchritudinem sapientiae, occurrat tibi pukhritudo iustitiae.

What shape is this? height is he? what color is it? Nihil horum est, et tamen est: nam si non esset, nec amaretur, nec merit laudaretur, nec amata nec laudata corde moribusque teneretur: nunc vero fiunt nomines sapientes; unde ieront, nisi esset sapientia? Porro autem, o homo, si sapientiam mam videre carnis oculis non potes, nec tali imaginatione cogitare quali corporalia cogitantur, sapientiae Dei audes ingerere humani corporis formam? 5. Quid etgo dicimus, fratres? Quomodo locutus est Pater Filio, quoniam Filius ait, Sicut docuit me Pater, haec loquor? Locutus est illi? Quando docuit Pater Filium, verba fecit, quomodo tu, quando

bras, how do you do when you teach your son? How to say many words with a single Verb? Did the Word of the Father apply his ears to the mouth of the Father? These are carnal things, which must be far from your heart. This is what I tell you, if you have understood what I have told you. Certainly I have spoken, my words have sounded, and with the sounds they hammered your ears, and through your ears they carried my opinion to your heart, if you have managed to understand me. Imagine one who has heard a man speaking in Latin, who has only listened, without understanding what he said. As for the sound emitted by my mouth, he who has not understood has perceived it as well as you. He heard the sound; the same syllables shook his ears, but produced nothing in his heart. Because? Because he didn't understand anything. You, however, did understand. Where did your insight come from? I only made noise in your ear; Did I turn on the light in your heart? Certainly, if what I said is true and you not only heard, but also understood this truth, there have been two things here, note them: hearing and understanding. Hearing was caused by me, and understanding, by whom? I spoke in your ears so that you would hear. Who spoke to your heart so that you would understand? Without a doubt, someone spoke and said something to your heart, so that not only this noise of words sounded in your ears, but also some truth descended into your heart. Someone spoke to your heart, but you do not see him. If you understood, brothers, something was said to your heart. God's gift is intelligence. Who said this in your heart, if you understood? He who says twelves filium tuum, verba facis? Quomodo facit verba Verb? Quae verba fine ieront only Verb? Vetbum enim Patris aures habuit ad os Patris? Carnalia sunt ista, pereant de cordibus vestris. Hoc enim dico, ecce si intellexistis quod ego dixi, ego certe locutus sum, et mea verba sonuerunt, sonisque aures pepuletunt, et per sensum auditus vestri ad cor sententiam perduxerunt, si intellexistis.

Facite aliquem audisse latinae linguae hominem, tantummodo audisse, nec tamen intellexisse quod dixi: quantum ad strepitum pertinet emissum ex ore meo, sic eius ille particeps factus est qui non intellexit, quomodo et vos; eum sonum audivit, eaedem syllabae aures eius percuserunt; sed in corde ipsius nihil genuerunt. Quate? Quia non intellexit. Vos autem si intellexistis, unde intellexistis? Ego ad autem sonui; numquid ego in corde lumen accendi? Procul dubio si verum est quod dixi, et hoc verum non solum audistis, verum etiam intellexistis; duae res ibi factae sunt, discernite illas, auditus et intellectus. Auditus per me factus est, intellectus per quem? Ego ad aurem dixi ut audiretis, ad cor vestrum quis dixit ut intelligeretis? Sine dubio aliquis et ad cor vestrum aliquid dixit, ut non solum strepitus iste verborum percuteiet aurem vesttam, sed etiam in cor vestrum aliquid descenderet veritatis: dixit aliquis et ad cor vesttum, sed non eum videtis; si intellexistis, frattes, dictum est et cordi vestro. Munus Dei est intelligentia. Quis

the Psalm: Give me understanding to know your commands. For example: the bishop spoke. What did he say? one asks. You answer what he said and add if he said the truth. Then another, who did not understand, says: What did he say or why do you praise him? They both heard me; For both I spoke, but for only one I said. If you allow me to compare small things with big things, because what are we compared to Him? I don't know what it is that God immaterially and spiritually works in us, which is neither the sound that pulses in the ear, nor the color that the eyes see, nor the smell that the nose feels, nor the flavor that the palate perceives, neither hard nor soft to the touch; However, it is something that is easy to feel and impossible to explain. If, then, God, as I was saying, speaks in our hearts without sounds, how does he speak to his Son? Think, brothers, think that in this way, if, as I said, the comparison of big things with other small things is allowed. Think like this. The Father spoke incorporeally to the Son, because incorporeally the Father begot the Son. But he did not teach him, as if he had fathered an unlearned Son. That he taught him is the same as saying that he begot him full of wisdom. And the same thing is: The Father taught me, that: He begot Me full of wisdom. If the nature of truth is simple, which few understand, being and knowing are the same in the Son. Who has the knowledge of who has the being. Not in such a way that it had first being and then knowledge, but in the way that begetting it gave it being, in the same way begetting it gave it knowledge; porhoc dixit in corde vestto, si intellexistis? Cui dicit Psalmus, Da mihi iniellectum, ut disccam maniata tua fPs 118.73). Verbi gratia, episcopus locutus est. Quid locutus est, aliquis ait? You answer quid locutus sit, et addis: Verum dixit. Tune alius qui non intellexit: Quid dixit, inquit, aut quid est quod laudas? Ambo me audierunt, ambobus ego dixi; sed uni ipsorum Deus dixit.

Si parva magnis comparare conceditur, quoniam nos ad eum quid sumus? tamen nescio quid incorporaliter et spíritualiter facit in nobis Deus, quod nec sonus est qui aurem percutiat, nec color qui oculis discernatur, nec odor est qui naribus capiatur, nec sapor qui faucibus iudicetur, nec durum et molle quod tangendo sentiatur: tamen aliquid est quod will feel facile est, I will explain the impossibility of this. Si ergo Deus, ut dicere coeperam, loquitur in cordibus nostris sine rang, quomodo loquitur Filio suo? Sic ergo, fratres, sic cogitate, quantum potestis, ut dixi, si licet parva magnis moda aliquo comparare; sic fuck yourself. Incorporaliter Pater locutus est Filio, quia incorporaliter Pater genuit Filium. Nec eum sic docuit quasi indoctum genuerit: sed hoc est eum docuisse, quod est scientem genuíse; et hoc est, docuit me Pater, quod est, scientem me genuit Pater. Si enim, quod pauci intelligunt, simplex est natura veritatis; hoc est Filio esse quod nosse. Ab illo ergo habet ut noverit, a quo habet ut sit: non ut prius ab illo esset, et ab illo postea nosset; sed quemadmodum illi gignendo dedit ut esset, sic gignendo dedit ut nosset: quia

that for the simple nature of truth, being is not one thing and knowing is another, but the same. 6. He said this to the Jews, and added: And he who sent me is with me. He had said the same thing before, but, because it is a very high thing, he frequently repeats: He sent me and he is with me. If he is with you, O Lord, one was not sent by the other, but you both came. And yet, despite being together, one is sent and another sends, because the mission is the incarnation, and the incarnation is only of the Son, not of the Father. The Father sent the Son, but was not separated from the Son. The Father did not cease to be there where he sent the Son. Where is he who made all things? Where is he who said: I fill heaven and earth? Is it that perhaps the Father is everywhere and the Son is not everywhere? Listen to the Gospel: I was in this world, and the world was made by Him. Then he who sent me, by whose command, as a father, I became incarnate, is with me, he did not leave me. Why didn't he leave me? He didn't leave me alone, he says, because I always do what he likes. That is equality, always, not of a beginning and continued, but without beginning and without end. For the generation of God has no temporal beginning, because by the Begotten the times were made. 7. When He said these things, many believed in Him. I hope that through my words many of those who otherwise thought they knew would understand and believe in Him! Perhaps there are some Arians among you. I dare not suspect that there are Sabellians, who say that the Father is the same as the Son. It is very old simplici, ut dictum est, naturae veritatis esse et nosse non est aliud atque aliud, sed hoc ipsum. 6. Dixit ergo ista Iudaeis, et addidit: Et qui me misit mecum est. lam hoc et ante dixetat, sed rem magnam assidue commemotat: misil me, et mecum est. Si etgo tecum est, or Domine, non unus ab alio missus est, sed ambo venistis. Et tamen eum ambo simul sint, unus missus est, alter misit: quoniam missio incarnatio est, et ipsa incarnatio Filii tantum est, non et Patris. Misit itaque Pater Filium, sed non recessit a Filio. Non enim quo misit Filium, non ibi etat Pater. Ubi enim non est qui fecit omnia? ubi non est qui dixit, Caelum et terram ego impleo? (Jer 23,24). Sed forte Pater ubique, et Filius non ubique est?

Evangelistam audi: In hoc mundo erat, et mundus per eum Cactus est (lo 1,10). Ergo, inquit, qui misit me, cuius auctorítate tanquam paterna incarnatus sum, mecum est, non me reliquit. Quare non me reliquit? Non me reliquit, inquit, solum quia ego quae plácitosunt ei, jacio sem-pet. Ipsa est aequalitas semper, non ex quodam initio et deinceps, sed sine initio, sine fine. Dei enim generatio non habet initium temporis, quia per genitum facta sunt tempora. 7. Haec illo loqaente, multi crediderunt in eum. Utinam et me loquente multi qui aliud sapiebant intelligant, et credant in eum. Quidam enim fortasse sunt in ist muhtitudine ariani. Non audeo suspicari esse sabernos qui ipsum Patrem dicunt esse qui Filius est: haetesis

This heresy has gradually become lifeless. That of the Arians, on the contrary, still seems to have some jerks, like that of a rotting corpse or, at most, of a man who is dying. It is advisable to liberate those who remain from it, as many have already been liberated. Certainly there were none in this city, but among the many pilgrims who have come to it, some of them also arrived. You see how, when the Lord said these things, many believed in Him. May God grant that, hearing my words, the Arians will believe, not in me, but with me. 8. So the Lord said to the Jews who had believed in Him: If you continue in my doctrine. It says remain, because you have already been initiated, you have already begun to be within it. That is to say: If you remain in the faith that has begun to take root in you, where will you arrive? Consider where such a beginning leads. You have already laid the foundations, take care of the finishing, and in this lowness discover another greatness. Faith is founded on humility. In vision, in immortality, in eternity, there is nothing humble; everything is greatness, everything is firm without weakness; Everything is stability without any attack from the enemy and without fear of losing it. Excelso is what is founded on faith and is not given importance, just as fools do not usually appreciate the foundations of a building. A large ditch is opened and the stones are thrown disorderly into it; There is no polish, no beauty. Nor does any beauty appear in the roots of the tree, but everything in the tree that delights you comes from the root. You contemplate the root and permaquippe ista nimis antiqua est, et paulatim eviscerata. Arianorum autem adhuc videtur habere aliquas motiones quasi cadaveris putrescentis; aut certe, ut multum, quasi hominis animam agents: oportet inde reliquos liberan, sicut inde multi liberati sunt. Et quidem ist civitas eos non habebat; sed posteaquam multi peregrini advenerunt, nonnulli et ipsi venerunt. Ecce haec Domino loquente multi Iudaei crediderunt in eum; ecce et me loquente Ariani credant, non in me, sed mecum. 8. Dicebat ergo Dominus ad eos qui crediderant in eum ludaeos: Si vos manseritis in -verbo meo. Ideo manseritis, quia initiati estis, quia et ibi esse coepistis.

Si manseritis, hoc est in fide quae in vobis esse credentibus coepit; what pervenietis? Vide quale initium, quo perducit. Amasti fundamentum, culmen attende, et ex ista humilitate alliam celsitudinem quaete. Fides enim humilitatem habet: cognitio et immortalitas et aeternitas non habet humilitatem, sed celsitudinem; erectionem, millam defectionem, aeternam stabilitatem, nullam ab inimico expugnatíonem, nullum deficiendí timorem. Magnum is quod incipit a fide; thirst contemnitur. Fundamentum solet etiam in aedificio ab imperitis contemni. Fossa fit grandis, lapides quoquo modo passim mittuntur; nulla ibi expolitio, nulla pulchritudo apparet: quomodo nec in arboris radice, non apparet aliqua pulchritudo; totum tamen quidquid te delec-
About the Gospel of Saint John

You need not be indifferent, you contemplate the tree and you are filled with admiration. Fool, what causes you admiration comes from the root, which has left you indifferent. You value the faith of believers little, because you lack scales to weigh it. Look where it goes and consider its value. The same Lord says in another place: If you have faith like a mustard seed. Could there be something smaller and more developed? Can there be anything more tiny and more fiery? Therefore, if you continue in my doctrine, in which you have already believed, where will you come? You will be true disciples of mine. And what use does this bring us? And you will know the Truth. 9. What did he promise to the believers, brothers? And you will know the truth. Well, hadn't they already known her when the Lord spoke? And if they had not known her, how did they believe? They did not believe because they had known her; They believed in order to know it, because we believe in order to know, we do not know in order to believe. What we are to know, neither eye has seen, nor ear has heard, nor has the heart imagined. Well, what is faith if not believing what you don't see? Faith is believing what you don't see; truth is seeing what you have believed, according to what He Himself says elsewhere. The Lord walked the earth to plant faith. He was a man, he had humbled himself, he was seen by everyone, but not known by everyone; He was despised by many, he was killed by the mob, pitied by few; However, not even those who pitied him recognized him for what he was. All this was like an initial definition of the faith and the future building, in view of which the Lord himself says in tat in arbore, de radice surrexit. Sed vides radicem, et non delectaris; vines arborem et miraris. Stulte, quod miraris, inde surrexit quo non delectaris. Parum aliquid videtur fides credentium, non habes stateiam unde appendas. Audi ergo quo perveniat, et vide quanta sit: sicut et ipse Dominus alio loco dicit, Si habueritis fidem sicut granum sinapis (Mt 17,19). Quid humilius, quid vehementius? quid minutius, quid ferventius? Ergo et vos, ait, si manseritis in verbo meo, in quo ctedidistis, quo perducemini? I will see disciple mei eritis. Et quid nobis prodest? Et cognoscetis veritatem. 9. Quid promittit credentibus, fratres? Et cognoscetis veritatem. Quid enim? non illam cognoverant, quando Dominus Ioquebatur? If not cognoverant, how crediderunt?

Non quia cognoverunt crediderunt, sed ut cognoscerent crediderunt. Credimus enim ut cognoscamus, non cognoscimus ut credamus. Quod enim cognituri sumus, nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascendit (Is 64:4; 1 Cor 2:9). Quid est enim fides, nisi credere quod non vides? Fides ergo est, quod non vides credere; veritas, quod credídísti vídere: sicut ipse quodam loco ait. Ideo Dominus prius ad faciendam fidem ambulavit in terra. Homo erat, humilis factus erat; ab omnibus videbatur, nec ab omnibus cojnoscebatur; a multis reprobabatur, a turba occidebatur, a paucis dolebatur: sed tamen et ab eis a quibus dolebatur, nondum sicut erat ag nos cébame.

another place: Whoever loves me keeps my commands, and whoever loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him. Those who heard him certainly saw him, and yet he promises them that they will see him if they love him. Thus it says here: You will know the truth. Well what? What you said, isn't it true? It is true, but it is still believed, it is not yet seen. If you remain in what you believe, you will reach what you have to see. Therefore Saint John the Evangelist himself says in his epistle: We are dear children of God, but what we will be does not yet appear. We already are, and we will still be something. There is a middle that separates; but there is a mediator who reconciles: the medium that separates is sin, and the mediator who reconciles is our Lord Jesus Christ, because there is one God and there is also one mediator between God and men, the man Jesus Christ. To remove the wall that separates, which is sin, He came as a mediator and became priest and victim. And because he became a victim for sin, offering himself as a burnt offering on the cross of his passion, the Apostle goes on to say, after having said: We beg you, in the name of Christ, to be reconciled to God, as if we were saying: how can we be reconciled? Him, he says, that is, Christ Himself, who knew no sin, made sin for us, so that in Him we might be the righteousness of God. Christ God himself, he says, who knew no sin, came in flesh, that is, in the likeness of sinful flesh; but in the flesh of sin without absolutely any sin, and that is why He became a true victim for sin, because He had no sin. 6. Perhaps some believe that I on my own have said that sin is a sacrifice for sin. Those who have read it, remember it; and those who have not read it, do not be slow, do not be slow, I say, in reading it, so that you may judge truly. they reconcile Deo. Quomodo autem reconciliamur, nisi solvatur quod inter nos et ipsum separat? Ait enim per prophetam: Nongravavit aurem ne auditat, sed peccata vestra separant inter vos et Deum (Is.59,1.2). Quia ergo non reconciliamur nisi ablato quod in medio est, et pósito quod in medio sit. Est enim medium separans, sed contra est mediator reconcilians; medium separans est peccatum, mediator reconcilians est Dominus lesus Christus: Unus enim Deus, et unus mediator Dei et hominum, homo Christus lesus (1 Tim 2,5). Ut ergo tollatur maceria separans quod est peccatum, venit ille mediator, et factus est sacrificium sacerdos ipse. Et quia sacrificium factus est pro peccato, offerens seipsum in holocaustum in cruz passionis suae, sequitur Apostolus et dicit, cum dixisset, Obsecramus pro Christo, reconcilian Deo: quasi diceremus, quomodo poterimus reconcilian?

Eum, inquit, id est ipsum Christum, qui non noverat peccatum, peccatum pro nobis fecit, ut nos simus iustitia Dei in ipso (2 Cor 5,20,21). Eum ipsum, inquit, Christum Deum, qui non noverat peccatum. Venit enim in carne, hoc est in similarityine carnis peccati (Rom 8:3), non tamen in carne peccati, non habens uüum omnino peccatum: et ideo factus est verum sacrificium pro peccato, quia nullum habebat ipse peccatum. 6. Sed forte de sensu meo dixi, quia peccatum sacrificium est pro peccato. Qui legerunt, agnoscant; qui non legerunt, non sint pigri: non sint, inquam, pigri ad legendum, ut veraces sint ad iudicandum. Cum de saciificiis enim praeciperet Deus offerendis pro peccato, in quibus
About the Gospel of Saint John

When God commanded to offer sacrifices for sin, in which the true atonement for sin was not given, but were a shadow of the future ones; the same sacrifices, the same victims, the same oblations, the same animals that were brought to be sacrificed for sin, whose blood was a figure of the blood of Christ, the Law calls them sin, to the point that in some places it is written that the sacrificial priests placed their hands on the head of sin, that is, on the head of the victim who sacrificed himself for sin. Such a sin, that is, such a sacrifice for sin, was made by Our Lord Jesus Christ, who knew no sin. 7. In all justice he delivers from the slavery of sin who says in the Psalm: I have become like a man forsaken by all, manumitted among the dead. Only He was free, because He had no sin. He himself says in the Gospel: Behold, the prince of this world comes, alluding to the devil, who was to come in the person of the Jews, his persecutors; Behold, he says, he is coming and will find nothing in me. And as if one could object: If he will find nothing in you, why should he kill you? He added: But so that everyone may know that I do the will of my Father, get up, let's get out of here. He says, I do not pay the death of my sin out of necessity, but in dying I fulfill the will of my Father, and in this I do more than I suffer, because, if I did not want to, I would not suffer either. Hear him say in another place: I have power to give my life and I have power to sacrificiis non erat expiatio peccatorum, sed umbra Futurerum, eadem ipsa sacrificia, easdem ipsas hostias, easdem ipsas victimas, eadem ipsa animalia quae admovebantur mactanda pro peccatis, in quorum sanguine sanguis ille figurabatur, peccata Lex appellat: usque adeo ut in quibusdam locis scriptum sit ita, ut priests immolaturiponerent manus suas super caput peccati, id est, super caput victimae immolandae pro peccato. Tale ergo peccatum, id est, sacrificium pro peccato, factus est Dominus noster Iesus Christus, qui non noverat peccatum. 7. Merito liberat ab hac servitute peccati ille qui dicit in Psalmis: Factus sum tanquam homo sine adiutorio, inter mortuos líber (Ps 87,5.6). Solus enim liber, quia non habebat peccatum. Ipse enim dicit in Gospel: Ecce venit princeps huius mundi, diabolum significans venturum in Iudaeis persecutoribus; ecce, inquit, venit et in me nihil inveniei (lo 14,30.31).

Non quomodo in eis quos occidit etiam iustos, invenit qualecumque peccatum, in me nihil inveniet. Et tanquam ei diceretur, si nihil in te inveniet, quare te occidet? Subiecit, et ait: Sed ut sciani omnes quia voluntatem Patris mei jacio, surgite, eamus bine. Non, inquit, mortem mei peccati necessitate persolvo, sed in eo quod moiioí, voluntatem Patris mei fació: plusque ibi fació quam patior, quia si nolIem, nec passus essem. Habes illum alio loco dicentem, Potestatem ha-

take it again. There we have him truly free among the dead. 8. Since he who commits sin is a slave to sin, listen to where we have the hope of freedom. The raven, he says, does not stay in the house forever. The house is the Church, the servant is the sinner. Many sinners enter the Church; but he did not say, The servant is not in the house; but: It does not remain in the house forever. Well, if there are to be no servants there, who will be there? When the righteous King, says the Scripture, sits on the throne, who can boast of having a pure heart or being free from all sin? Full of terror he left us, my brothers, saying that the servant does not remain in the house forever. And he adds: But the son remains forever. Will Christ be alone in his house? Will there be no one with him? Whose head will it be, if there is no body? Is the Son the body and the head? Not in vain did he leave us fear and hope: fear, so as not to love sin, and hope, so as not to distrust achieving its forgiveness; because whoever commits sin is a servant of sin, and the servant does not remain in the house forever. What hope is left for us, who cannot be without sin? Hear where your hope is: The son remains forever. If the Son gives you freedom, then you will be truly free. This, brothers, is our hope: to see ourselves liberated by him who is truly free, and, by liberating us, he makes us servants, because we were servants of concupiscence and with freedom we become servants of the Cabeo Pondi Animam Meam, et Potestatem Babeo Iterum Sumendi Eam (ibid. 10,18). Ecce I will see in mortuis liber. 8. Cum ergo omnis qui facit peccatum, servus sit peccati, quae sit spes nobis libertatis, audite. Servus autem, inquit, non manet in domo in aeternum. Ecclesia est domus, servus peccator est. Intrant multi in Ecclesiam peccatores. Non ergo dixit, Servus non est in domo; sed, non manet in domo in aeternum. Si ergo nullus ibi servus etit, quis ibi erit? Cum enim rex iustus sederit in throne, sicut Scriptuia loquitur, quis gloriabitur castum se habere cor? aut quis gloriabitur mundum se esse a sin? (Prov 20,8.9). Multum nos terruit, o fiatres mei, saying, Servus non manet in domo in aeternum, Adiungit autem, et dicit, Vilius autem manet in aeternum. Ergo solus in domo sua erit Christus? nullus illi populus cohaerebit? Cui etit caput, si non erit corpus? An forte totum hoc Filius, caput et Corpus?

Ñon enim sine causa et terruit, et spem dedit: tetruit, ne peccatum amaremus; spem dedit, ne de peccati solutione diffideremus: Omnis, inquit, qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati. Servus autem non manet in domo in aeternum. Quae etgo nobis spes est, qui non sumus sine peccato? Audi spem tuam; Filius manet in aeternum. Si ergo vos Filius liberaverit, tune veré liberi erilis. Haec spes nostra est fratres ut a libero liberemur, et liberando serves us faciat: seivi enim eramus cupiditatis, liberatj serví efficimuí charitatis. Hoc et Apostolus di-
